structured_output.what_is_happening: FOOMS (7zJ4...) is a 35-minute-old PumpSwap pair. It was not a pump.fun migration: migrated_unix is 0, the launchpad field is empty, and the description reads "Created on https://unorich.com". It has done about $6.3M of volume on a roughly $185k market cap, which is 23x turnover in an hour. Price is up about 112-125% in the hour and slipped 3-6% in the last 5 minutes. GeckoTerminal shows 1,732 unique buyers but only 57 unique sellers, and those 57 made about 3,900 sells, roughly 70 each. That is the signature of volume bots and a farm, not organic trading. Liquidity ($263k) is higher than market cap, 72% of supply sits in a pool whose LP is unlocked (0% locked, burn ratio 0), and GMGN tags 49 bundler wallets. At least six same-name FOOMS tokens were launched within about 3 hours. Two of them (K3dBv..., $2.28M of h1 volume, and FoyeQ...) now show $0 liquidity, and PSuzun... is running the same volume pattern ($8.8M in h1). This looks like a serial launch-and-pull cluster built around the name "fooms". I found no organic social presence.

The only other hits are unrelated: an Instagram food account, a university research group, and the AI 'foom' concept. There is no website (unorich.com failed TLS) and the X handle is just a search link.

This is a self-created PumpSwap pool, not a pump.fun graduation, so there are no curve protections.
The volume is bot-driven, so real demand is unknown.

It is part of a serial cluster of FOOMS clones, some already drained, and has no narrative or social footprint. A rug within 6 hours is the most likely outcome. A 2x from about $180k would need the operator to keep pumping rather than pull.
